meta.description: Simulation study for 'Where Criticism Ends' (synthetic data only; no real survey data).
meta.seed_scheme: numpy SeedSequence([base_seed, experiment_index, cell keys..., rep])
meta.code_sha256_16_note: per experiment: experiments.<E>.code_sha256_16 (hashes of the code that produced it)
meta.estimation: Limited-information: two-step polychoric correlations (Olsson 1979) with influence-function asymptotic covariance; DWLS fit (diagonal weights) of the bifactor model in the IRT (theta) parameterisation; sandwich SEs; nonparametric bootstrap for ECV intervals.

E2.description: Two groups (n=1500 each), DIF on Israel-related items I1, I2 (uniform) and I3 (non-uniform); focal-group latent means (G,S,I) = (0.3, 0, 0.3); strategies: naive (full invariance), oracle (true DIF items free), free-baseline with anchor sets (correct, contam1, contam2) and the pre-registered procedure (Wald + BH q=0.05 + expected-score effect size >= 0.25, then refit); stereotype-only anchors S1-S4 with mu_I, sigma_I fixed (rem:id-anchor-S). Naive = concurrent calibration with equal group sizes (rem:id-concurrent). Focal ECV per def:boundary (with focal factor variances).
E2.seeds: SeedSequence([base, 2, round(100 kappa), rep]); population weights: [base, 2, 999, round(100 kappa)]

E3.description: One sensitive item, threshold-shift model of social desirability (def:le-shift, normal ogive): pi = 0.30, pi^D = 0.20 (SDB = 0.10) unless false endorsement phi > 0. Part A: split design, equal vs Neyman (thm:design(a)) vs pilot plug-in allocation; SDB_S (eq:le-split) and a covariate-adjusted version. Part B: paired design (thm:joint-sdb(b),(c)), post-stratified SDB_PS and combined eta-hat, under monotonicity (phi = 0) and false endorsement (phi = 0.02), vs the split design. Part C: control-list menu J in 2..6, binary within-pair correlation rho in {0, -0.6}, floor/ceiling probability kc = kf in {0, 0.5} (thm:design(c),(d)).

E4.description: MRP of the area mean of G (50 areas, 32 demographic cells per area, differential non-response by age and education); score y = theta_G + N(0, s_m^2) (conditionally unbiased); MRP = REML random-intercept model on y + poststratification (eq:mrp), which in this Gaussian setting is the latent regression with measurement error integrated out; two-step EAP = the same MRP on posterior-mean scores under one common prior (prop:eap); direct = area sample mean (unweighted and national cell-weighted). A new population is drawn in every replication.

E5.description: Population index P(agree with >= k of 8 S items) by group vs the latent mean difference delta of G; random uniform DIF b_j^(1) = b_j^(0) + N(0, s^2) sd_j on the S items; reversal = sign(index difference) != sign(delta). Exact (quadrature) for 1000 random configurations per (s, |delta|); finite-sample check with n = 1000 per group.
E5.seeds: SeedSequence([base, 5, round(100 s), round(100 |delta|)]); finite sample [base, 5, 500 + round(100 s), round(100 delta), rep]

E1.description: Recovery of loadings, item-level ECV, boundary set (tau=0.5) and S-I correlation; single group, bifactor DGP (probit GRM), DWLS on polychorics, bootstrap percentile and logit-Wald (sandwich) 95% intervals.
E1.seeds: data: SeedSequence([base, 1, cfg_index, n, rep]).spawn(2)[0]; bootstrap: .spawn(2)[1]

E1b.description: As E1 for a design close to proportionality (rem:id-heterogeneity): S-block ECVs 0.65-0.75 (common communality 0.55), n_I = 3, so Assumption id-het holds only weakly in S and fails in I.
